targets.title: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards
targets.native_Description_identity_context: We prove the k403,a observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller: the signed area product of the original orbit's origin pedal and origin antipedal is phase independent for every primitive least odd period in a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strict confocal elliptical caustic. All admitted coprime stars are included and every real antipedal intersection is finite. The construction-specific proof distinguishes coincident and opposite complex endpoints, cancels incident double poles and identifies the odd-period quotient lattice. The earlier credited origin-pedal trace supplies the complementary factor. A direct circular extension and an exact same-caustic four-periodic counterexample delimit the theorem. The verification archive contains the standalone LaTeX source, exact algebra and reflected-orbit certificates, independent high-precision geometry and near-pole diagnostics, full receipt comparisons, source hashes, mathematical audits and bounded priority reports. The original observation, prior campaign pedal argument and classical elliptic/cyclic-identity methods are credited. No historical-firstness certificate is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification, literature research, coding, writing and internal adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

targets.title: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
targets.native_Description_identity_context: For a fixed odd least-period elliptic billiard family with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove constancy of the product of the signed straight-edge areas obtained by unit inversion of the outer tangent-polygon vertices about the two original billiard foci. Every admissible coprime star turning number, the critical triangular case and fixed repeated traversals are included. This proves the assertion conjectured as k904,a in Reznik--Garcia--Koiller arXiv2004.12497v11, Table10 (earlier v10 label k808,a). The proof gives the explicit inverse-edge factorization, cancels double principal parts in the cyclic area sum, and applies the classical complementary zero/pole divisor argument on a compact torus. Stachel canonical coordinates, established Jacobi and cyclic elliptic identities, and earlier complex billiard and complementary-area techniques are credited. Original-vertex inverse areas and outer-locus-focus inversions are distinct targets. No exact earlier general proof was verified in two independent bounded priority audits; historical novelty remains undetermined. The final journal text of The talented Mr. Inversive Triangle was subscription-limited, open author versions were read, and selected-passage and unresolved-source limitations are preserved. No first-proof, absolute-priority, new general elliptic-method or current-worldwide-open claim is made. The deposit includes a concise research note and a portable source/verification archive preserving original submissions, exact controls, separately labeled numerical diagnostics and authored audit records. Finite checks support rather than replace the universal proof. AI tools were used extensively in solving, writing, computation, source investigation and independent internal adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification.

targets.title: Polynomial compatibility on the Boolean cube from disjoint-support separators
targets.native_Description_identity_context:
A complete affirmative deduction for Austrin's exact two-polynomial question, OWR 9/2025 printed p. 445 (30006210 / OWR-14299088-012). For every positive n,d and nonzero real multilinear f,g of degree at most d on the uniform sign cube, all full-norm relative coordinate influences at most 1/(4096d^8) guarantee a common nonzero vertex. Disjoint supports force maximum relative influence at least1/(1024d^8). The denominator includes the constant Fourier coefficient; arbitrary common zeros are allowed. Constants/exponent are not claimed optimal. General distribution formulations, other groups/measures and approximate supports are outside the asserted theorem.

This four-page note is an explicit target-specific application of the established Li-Li-Li-Liu 2026 disjoint-support separator and O'Donnell-Saks-Schramm-Servedio 2005 section3.3 Eq(6) real covariance inequality, with the classical Markov/Bernoulli presentation credited to Kothari and coauthors. Neither the separator nor covariance inequality is claimed new. The complete square-density conversion and extracted depth 16d^4 are supplied.

Extensive bounded primary priority audits found no earlier recorded complete target-specific deduction in the bodies inspected. They do not certify novelty, first discovery/publication or global current openness. The full ePrint 2022/218 and full 2023/570 followup were inaccessible; the official CRYPTO 2022 conference version was read and separately pinned. Other historical coverage and procedural-independence limits are documented. Dates and negative searches do not certify firstness or causal independence.

The source archive preserves all ten original PR artifacts, three distinct mathematical audits, three priority approaches, root checks, and a portable offline standard-library verification runner. Four exact integer/rational programs run in ordinary and optimized modes with all mathematical fields compared exactly and forty actual incorrect-result failures. Finite checks supplement the universal proof; they are not arbitrary-dimensional enumeration or formal proof certificates. Third-party source bodies are excluded.
